_comment: ROUND 2 (2026-09-03) — one question: are glm-5.3 and qwen3.8-max actually
worse, or were they never given a fair run?
The answer turned out to be 'never given a fair run', three times over, and
every fault was ours:
1. qwen3.8-max was BOTH a candidate and the judge in round 1. On `assess`
it came back with no quality score and then won on token count.
2. glm-5.3 was banned from reflex/dialogue/digest by a catalog rule that
read 'rejects enable_thinking:false' as 'always reasons'. It is not the
same thing: at reasoning_effort:low it returns ZERO reasoning tokens.
3. glm-5.3's http 400 on `assess` was never about reasoning at all — the
lookback call sends a system message and nothing else, and ZHIPU/GLM-5.3
answers `messages 参数非法` to that shape. Our own request bug.
And the first attempt at this round was itself void: the judge was
qwen3.7-max, the assess class sends reasoning_effort 'max', and that model
rejects the word 'max' (it wants 'xhigh'). Every judge call 400'd and the
report still printed a recommendation. routebench now refuses to recommend a
judged class with no quality data.
So glm-5.3 is now a candidate in every class it is eligible for, which is
all of them. It is the fastest model in the catalog by a wide margin on
compose and review (2.6-4.1s, 100% structural) — the open question is
whether it can hold judgement at that speed, and only the judge answers that.
